messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Upcoming changes to Shiny API
parts:
Hello Shiny users -

In the development version of Shiny on github, we've merged in a branch that makes some changes to the API. Your old code should continue to work, but it will result in messages about deprecated usage being printed to the console. There will be a bit of short-term pain in switching to the new API, but we think it's worthwhile, because the new interface is somewhat simpler, and because it offers a better mapping between the names and concepts.

If you like being on the cutting edge, please install this version on your local machine and test it out on your apps!
  library('devtools')
  install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

You can also install it on your account on Glimmer by connecting to RStudio server and installing from there. If you do so, then your apps will use your installed version of Shiny; if not, they will continue to use the system's installed version of Shiny, 3.1. (You may have to put 'library(shiny)' at the top your app's .R files for this to work, though.)


Here's what has changed:

* `reactive()` takes expressions as input, instead of functions. Here's an example:
  # Old style
  reactive(function() { ... })
  # New style
  reactive({ ... })

* `observe() also takes expressions instead of functions:
  # Old style
  observe(function() { ... })
  # New style
  observe({ ... })

* `reactiveText`, `reactivePlot`, and so on, have been replaced with `renderText`, `renderPlot`, etc. They also now take expressions instead of functions.
  # Old style
  reactiveText(function() { ... })
  # New style
  renderText({ ... })



If for some reason you want to save an unevaluated expression in a variable and then give it to, `reactive()`, `renderText()`, and so on, you can quote the expression and then use the quote=TRUE option:
  my_expr <- quote({ input$num + 1 })
  renderText(my_expr, quote=TRUE)


This should cover most use cases, although it's possible you might still run into some hurdles if you're doing tricky stuff with Shiny. If you still have problems migrating, please feel free to ask about it on this mailing list.


When we release the next version of Shiny, we'll also update the tutorial pages to reflect the new API.

-Winston
